title: Choose the visual world for the RevX landing page
question: The roll assigned Instrument Cluster. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Instrument Cluster
options.lineage: a car's night-lit dashboard: gauges, tell-tale lamps, the message-centre readout
options.thesis: RevX is the moment the check-engine lamp comes on and you finally get a real readout.
options.viewport: A full-width cluster: the seven loop steps as a tell-tale row, a message centre running the demo diagnosis, and Open RevX as the start button.
options.risk: Near-black plus one glowing accent is a known AI look, and skeuomorphic gauges tip into kitsch if glow is sprayed instead of earned.

raised.raise: Total palette commitment: the page lives under one night-drive light (black glass, sky backlight, amber warning) with no stray colour anywhere.
Committed vs candidate is a line state: the chosen cause or quote renders solid and lit, alternates stay dashed and dim.
Billing order is hierarchy: ranked causes and quotes are set strictly by rank, size stepping down with no ties.
One complete state vocabulary for every control: unlit, lit, flashing warning, and dimmed-not-yet-wired for roadmap items.
Every section leads with one demonstrating object (a lamp, a readout, a dial), and text only confirms what it shows.

options.label: Shop Repair Order
options.lineage: the carbonless triplicate repair order every shop counter fills out
options.thesis: Every post becomes the repair order a good shop would write, and both sides sign it.
options.viewport: A giant repair order filling itself in: the customer complaint box takes the intake, the technician's findings box takes the AI diagnosis, and Open RevX is the stamp.
options.risk: Paper-form worlds are a familiar landing-page move, and it leaves the app's dark identity behind entirely.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.lineage: a CRT oscilloscope on a bench
options.thesis: The noise you record becomes a trace the diagnosis reads off a graticule.
options.viewport: A ten-division graticule with the recorded brake grind as a live waveform and cause markers locking onto it.
options.case: Fuses well with the audio-recording feature and wins on product clarity, but owners don't recognise a scope the way they recognise their dashboard.
options.risk: Reads as an engineering tool, not a car-owner's world.

options.label: Zoot Handbill
options.thesis: RevX billed like a dance-hall night, owners and mechanics as headliners.
options.case: Loses on both axes: it can't show diagnosis or matching working.
options.risk: A costume of a culture the product doesn't serve directly.
options.kept: Billing order as strict hierarchy for ranked causes and quotes.

options.label: Wit Poster
options.thesis: Each feature told as one visual pun.
options.viewport: One pun image owning the sheet.
options.case: Loses on both axes: charming, but not car culture and hides the mechanism.
options.risk: Whimsy undercuts trust in a repair decision.
options.kept: Each section leads with one demonstrating object.

options.label: Indoor Sun
options.thesis: One amber light flattening the whole page.
options.case: Loses on both axes: atmosphere without a product.
options.kept: Total palette commitment under a single light.

options.label: Sewing Pattern
options.viewport: A tissue layout with numbered pieces.
options.case: Loses on both axes: wrong world for car owners and mechanics.
options.kept: Solid line for the committed choice, dashed for candidates.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.case: Loses on both axes: retro computing, not cars.
options.kept: One complete state vocabulary for every control.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The app's own dark garage look, as a classic app landing page done at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Garage photo hero, wordmark, tagline, two CTAs, phone mockup at right, then a three-step how-it-works.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other app landing page by design.
